Senses.Explanation: The thirty-two marks of the perfected body, carried by the records as the visible measure that mind is set against. Mazu Daoyi, quoted in the Mirror of the School, reads the sutra's marks as born from thought and turns them into proof that the mind-made body is the house the teaching uses; Guxue Zhenzhe counts the marks among everything that fails to appear once the heart's beings flow on; Zhuanyu Guanheng tells his correspondent that at the breakthrough one may treat the marks as a dung-chunk and the dung-chunk as the marks; and Zhongfeng Mingben traces the Seeing debate back to Ananda's claim to see the marks with his eyes. Zhanran Yuancheng reads the Devadatta chapter so that the marks are won through the bad friend on the non-path; Yongming Yanshou's own collection lists the marks as the twenty-fourth benefit of the western land; Jifei Ruyi's eulogy verse hands Ananda a sweetness that is one mark short of the thirty-two; and Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen's endowment inscription renews the marks in gold leaf on the temple's statue.
